From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Fwd: Production timeouts and 5xx/429 spikes — immediate help needed

Summary of what we see (quick RCA):
- Timeline: ~08:25 PDT increased request fanout from FinAPI (sudden traffic burst + aggressive retry policy on their side).
- Symptom: queue saturation on inference workers -> head-of-line requests started timing out -> client retries amplified load -> ~08:28 system-level threadpool exhaustion on a subset of instances -> 429 throttles and then 5xx from overloaded model processes.
- Autoscaler behavior: scale-out started at ~08:30 but did not bring enough capacity until ~08:38 due to slow container startup and model cold-start sequence.
- Alerting gap: we have an alert for CPU and node failures, but no alert threshold for sustained 5xx ratio over a rolling 15m window tied to traffic spikes; our 5xx alerts trigger only on host-failure patterns.

Immediate mitigations we applied (08:40-08:50):
- Tuned the adaptive rate limiter to be more aggressive for the affected tenant pattern.
- Temporarily moved FinAPI to a hotspot-mitigation pool with pinned warm instances (reduced cold starts).
- Added a temporary per-tenant request cap to prevent single-tenant retry storms.

What caused the amplification: combination of client retry behavior + no backpressure propagation to client + autoscaler cold-start latency. We also found a bug in our rate limiter where "burst" tokens were not being deducted under certain multi-threaded paths — this allowed sudden fanout to bypass limits until our sampling detected the anomaly.

I've started a draft postmortem (attached) with metrics and heap snapshots. Next steps for postmortem: runbook updates, add rolling 5xx ratio alert, SLO tuning, and investigate faster warm pool strategies or model snapshotting to reduce cold-starts.

Jonas
Principal SW Eng, Serving Runtime

Attachments: postmortem-draft.md

From: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, evelyn_hart@redwood.ai, laura.jensen@finapi.com
Date: 2026-06-18T11:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Production timeouts and 5xx/429 spikes — immediate help needed

Quick operational note and proposed action items:
1) Hotfix (applied 10:55 PDT) — patched adaptive rate limiter to avoid token miscount in multi-thread case. Patch: hotfix-params.patch attached.
2) Short-term mitigation (<=2 hours):
   - Enforce a stricter per-tenant QPS cap and apply exponential backoff guidance to FinAPI.
   - Move FinAPI to prewarmed pool while we validate autoscaler changes.
3) Medium-term (1-2 weeks):
   - Add a rolling 5xx/429 ratio alert (1m/5m/15m windows with escalation thresholds).
   - Create an SRE-authored runbook for retry storms (includes steps: throttle, warm pool, fallback model, notify).
   - Tune autoscaler warm-start and model snapshotting experiment to reduce cold start from ~6s to target <2s.
4) Long-term (quarter):
   - Backpressure propagation API (so client-side retries can be informed of server load).
   - Capacity planning: recommend a committed buffer of 20% for high-variance tenants like FinAPI.

Request for approvals:
- Neha/Marissa: propose a $15k service credit to FinAPI given impact and duration; need sales/billing sign-off.
- Rishi/Evelyn: ask for green light to prioritize autoscaler warm pool improvements in the next sprint.

I'll follow up with a crisp runbook draft by EOD and a timeline for the autoscaler experiment.

-Sean
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference

Laura — thank you for escalating and for the quick mitigation on your side. We sincerely apologize for the outage and the operational pain this caused your customers.

Summary & ask:
- What happened: transient client retry storm + a rare rate-limiter bug -> queue saturation -> autoscaler lag -> elevated 429/5xx and user-visible timeouts.
- What we did: hotfix applied to rate limiter, moved you to prewarmed pool, temporary per-tenant caps in place.
- Next steps: runbook + rolling 5xx alert will be in place by 2026-06-19 EOD. Autoscaler warm-start experiment slated for next sprint; we'll share a roadmap by Friday.

Compensation proposal: we propose a $15,000 service credit for the incident window and follow-up verification. If that is acceptable, we will start the credit workflow immediately and provide a DocuSign acceptance link.

Would you like us to schedule a 30-minute technical review tomorrow to walk through the fixes and the postmortem draft?

Again, very sorry — we take incidents like this seriously.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
